title: Triage the application route: own portal, Parcoursup, or DAP
institutions: All 8 programmes in the Pave France dataset
duration_realistic: 1-2 hours, at the very start
what_happens: France has three separate undergraduate entry systems and a counselor must decide which one applies before anything else. DAP (Demande d'Admission Prealable) is for first-year licence at PUBLIC universities and schools of architecture, runs 1 Oct-15 Dec inside Etudes en France, and applies to NONE of the eight programmes in this dataset. Parcoursup is for holders of the FRENCH baccalaureate (and is the registration route for the SESAME competitive exam used by SKEMA's Global BBA, emlyon's Global BBA and EDHEC's French-bac route) - so it does not apply to a CBSE/ISC student either. All eight programmes here are entered through the institution's OWN portal: Sciences Po admissions portal, Ecole Polytechnique's portal, EDHEC's own account system, MySKEMApply, emlyon's online admission test, ESSEC's portal (Global BBA and the ESSEC x CentraleSupelec BSc), and - for the HEC Paris x Bocconi BASc - Bocconi University's portal.
the_trap: Counselors who have read a generic 'study in France' guide put an Indian student into DAP or tell them to wait for Parcoursup. Both are dead ends for this dataset: DAP is public-university licence only and Parcoursup is French-bac only. The student loses the school's own round deadlines - which fall between September and March - while waiting for a portal that will never open for them.
exact_quote: Students with a French or European Baccalaureat use Parcoursup plus 'Etudes en France'; others submit a DAP (Preliminary Admission Request) through 'Etudes en France'. For 2026/2027 DAP registration ran 1 October - 15 December 2025.

title: Check the campus and track are actually 100% English-taught
duration_realistic: 1 hour
what_happens: Four of the eight entries carry an English-only sub-route that is narrower than the programme name suggests. Sciences Po's Bachelor of Arts is completable in English only at Le Havre, Menton (English track) and Reims - the Paris campus is French-taught, and the student applies to a CAMPUS, not to a major (the two majors are chosen in Year 2). EDHEC's English-only route is the Global Business track (Nice, then UCLA Extension and NTU Singapore) at EUR 23,900/year; the cheaper Business Management track at EUR 15,900/year requires French. emlyon's Global BBA is delivered in 'French or English'. SKEMA's Global BBA runs from Lille or Sophia Antipolis, not Paris.
the_trap: A no-French student is placed on Sciences Po Paris or EDHEC's Business Management track because the fee or the city looked better. The admission is valid, the degree is not completable in English, and the student discovers it after the deposit is paid and the visa file is built around that institution.
exact_quote: Taught entirely in English, the Global Business Track... | 'This track welcomes applicants proficient in French and English' (Business Management track).

title: English proof: required at some schools, explicitly optional at others
duration_realistic: 2-6 weeks if a test is needed (book, sit, receive score)
what_happens: The eight programmes do not share a language rule. Ecole Polytechnique requires a certificate unless the last two years of school were in English: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 90 / Cambridge CAE-CPE 176. ESSEC (both the Global BBA and the ESSEC x CentraleSupelec BSc) requires TOEIC 850 / TOEFL iBT 90 / IELTS Academic 6.5 / Cambridge B2 First 175, waived if the last 2 years were taught entirely in English, and refuses tests older than two years. HEC x Bocconi requires proof of B2. SKEMA requires a score from an official test for Year 1 entry but publishes NO minimum. Sciences Po states that attaching a certificate is entirely optional. EDHEC runs its own online English assessment for shortlisted candidates and treats an external certificate as optional.
the_trap: Two opposite mistakes. (1) A student skips the test because 'Sciences Po says it's optional' and then cannot apply to Polytechnique or ESSEC in the same season - IELTS slots in India during October-January fill weeks ahead. (2) A student sits the test in Class XI to be safe; ESSEC will not accept a score older than two years at the point of application. Note also that the French VISA file does not require an English or French test at all - the test is purely an admissions requirement.
exact_quote: Attaching proof of language proficiency (such as language tests) at the time of application is entirely optional.

title: CBSE/ISC Class XII recognition - there is no French APS or Anabin
duration_realistic: 0 for these eight schools; 2-4 months only if a comparability statement is separately demanded
what_happens: France has no pre-admission verification body equivalent to Germany's APS and no public grade-conversion table equivalent to Anabin. Each institution judges the Indian school-leaving certificate itself against the French baccalaureat standard: ESSEC asks for 'an international high school diploma equivalent to the French Baccalaureate' with grades 'way above the average with consistent or increasing results'; HEC x Bocconi asks only for a 'valid secondary school diploma (national or international) suitable for access to Bachelor programs'. None of the eight publishes a CBSE or ISC percentage minimum. Where a formal statement is wanted, France's ENIC-NARIC centre (France Education International) issues an attestation de comparabilite through its Phoenix platform - but none of these eight requires it for admission, and the French consulate does not require it for the student visa.
the_trap: Counselors invent cut-offs. Every CBSE/ISC percentage, IB score and A-level grade circulating for these eight programmes (IB 38 for Sciences Po, IB 34 for EDHEC and ESSEC, CBSE 85% for HEC) is absent from the schools' own pages - the Pave verification pass of 12 September 2026 marked them invented. The opposite trap is starting a four-month ENIC-NARIC comparability file nobody asked for and missing the school's round in the meantime.
exact_quote: Requirement is an international high school diploma equivalent to the French Baccalaureate with 'good grades... way above the average with consistent or increasing results'.

title: Apply on the school's own portal - and apply in an EARLY round, not the last one
duration_realistic: 3-6 weeks to assemble the file; rounds run Sept 2026 - June 2027 for the Sept 2027 intake
what_happens: Every one of the eight runs its own rounds, and the published 2027-intake calendars differ sharply. Sciences Po: applications open mid-September 2026; apply by 4 Nov 2026 (results mid-Jan 2027), by 13 Jan 2027 (results early April), or by 1 Mar 2027 (results early May); application fee EUR 150, non-refundable. Ecole Polytechnique: Round 1 17 Sep-20 Oct 2026, Round 2 21 Oct 2026-6 Jan 2027, Round 3 7 Jan-8 Feb 2027 at 2 PM CET; fee EUR 105. EDHEC International BBA: five rounds - R1 closes 3 Nov 2026 (results 17 Dec 2026), R2 7 Jan 2027 (results 18 Feb), R3 11 Feb 2027 (results 25 Mar), R4 1 Apr 2027 (results 20 May), R5 8 Jun 2027 (results 2 Jul 2027); fee EUR 100. HEC Paris x Bocconi: R1 closes 29 Sep 2026 (results 11 Nov 2026), R2 26 Jan 2027 (results 15 Mar), R3 27 Apr 2027 (results 27 May), submitted through BOCCONI's portal. ESSEC Global BBA and ESSEC x CentraleSupelec: 4-5 rounds roughly Oct-Apr, deadlines at 12 PM Paris time; fee EUR 100 (Cergy). SKEMA: rolling, a deadline every 15th of the month via MySKEMApply, decisions in about 4 weeks, September and January intakes. emlyon Global BBA: a single long application window with admission sessions organised regularly through to July.
the_trap: Applying in the last round. This is the single most expensive mistake in the French chain, because the Etudes en France pre-consular file cannot even be opened until the unconditional acceptance letter exists, and Campus France India tells students to submit at least three months before the intake. EDHEC's Round 5 result lands 2 July 2027 for a September 2027 start - roughly eight weeks to run EEF, the academic interview, VFS and visa processing that Sciences Po itself says takes two to three months. Rounds are also not equal in supply: EDHEC's Global Business track carries a 'Limited number of places available' note.
exact_quote: Round 1 Application deadline: from 1st October to 3rd November 2026... Round 5 Application deadline: from 6 April to 8 June 2027... Admission results: Thursday 2nd July 2027. Application fees are 100 EUR.

title: Sit the school's own test or interview - no SAT, no national entrance exam
duration_realistic: 2-8 weeks between submission and the interview slot
what_happens: None of the eight uses a French national entrance exam for an Indian applicant, and only one wants an American test. Sciences Po: a graded file (school exam results /20, academic performance /20, three written motivation answers /10) plus a 25-minute remote interview, together scored out of 100. Ecole Polytechnique: a mandatory ~50-minute remote interview conducted entirely in English. EDHEC: shortlisted candidates take the Emage-me personality test, an online English assessment and an online interview. ESSEC Global BBA: a 30-minute interview in front of two examiners. ESSEC x CentraleSupelec: a COMPULSORY online mathematics test taken after the application is submitted, plus a possible interview. emlyon: a four-stage online admission test ending in a deferred video interview where each question is timed. SKEMA: file plus admissions interview. HEC x Bocconi is the exception: 'Take an official SAT/ACT test or the Bocconi online admissions test', plus a video interview.
the_trap: Two traps. (1) The SESAME competitive exam is repeatedly mis-sold to Indian students for EDHEC, ESSEC, SKEMA and emlyon - SESAME is the FRENCH-baccalaureate route only, registered through Parcoursup, and an Indian applicant neither needs nor can use it. (2) The tests that do exist are triggered AFTER submission and are timed: ESSEC x CentraleSupelec's maths test and emlyon's timed video interview arrive with little notice, and students who applied and then stopped checking email miss the window.
exact_quote: 30 minutes in front of two examiners. SESAME competitive exam applies ONLY to French Baccalaureate holders.

title: Accept the offer and pay the enrolment deposit - the clock starts here
institutions: EDHEC, ESSEC, Sciences Po, Polytechnique, SKEMA, emlyon
duration_realistic: Deposit typically due 2 weeks after the admission decision
what_happens: The admission letter is what unlocks the whole visa chain, but it normally arrives attached to a fast, large, non-refundable payment. EDHEC: 'A 5,000 EUR deposit must be made prior to enrollment: two weeks after being admitted by credit card online.' ESSEC: a non-refundable deposit of EUR 5,500 (or MAD 25,000 in Rabat), deducted from tuition. Non-EU students at EDHEC must then pay the balance by wire transfer - direct debit is not available to them. The document the consulate will want is the UNCONDITIONAL acceptance letter; an offer still conditional on Class XII results is not enough to open the visa file.
the_trap: A EUR 5,000-5,500 deposit falls due within fourteen days, on a card, before any visa exists - and it is non-refundable if the visa is later refused. Families who budgeted only for tuition instalments are caught, and the offer lapses. Separately, students holding a conditional offer wait for the final marksheet before starting Etudes en France and lose four to six weeks at exactly the point in the year when they cannot afford to.
exact_quote: A 5,000 EUR deposit must be made prior to enrollment: two weeks after being admitted by credit card online.

title: HEC Paris x Bocconi only: this degree starts in ITALY, so the first visa is Italian
institutions: HEC Paris x Bocconi BASc in Data, Society and Organisations
duration_realistic: Adds a full parallel Italian admission and visa track in Year 1
what_happens: Semesters 1 to 3 of this double degree are at Bocconi in Milan and only semesters 4 to 6 are at HEC Paris. The application is submitted through Bocconi's portal and the admission decision is issued by Bocconi. The consequence for an Indian student is that the first immigration step is an ITALIAN study visa (Universitaly pre-enrolment and the Italian consulate in India) - Etudes en France, Campus France India and the French VLS-TS play no part in Year 1. The French leg is dealt with about eighteen months later, from Italy. The EU intra-mobility notification that normally covers a student moving between member states (CERFA 15972*01, 'Demande de mobilite en France d'un etudiant autorise a sejourner en Europe') is capped at 360 days, so three semesters at HEC exceed it and a full French residence title is the likely route.
the_trap: A counselor prepares a France file - Campus France, EEF fee, French proof of funds - for a student who is flying to Milan. Conversely, the France leg is then treated as automatic because 'it's one degree': it is not, and because the mobility notification only covers 360 days the three HEC semesters will need a separate French permit. Confirm the exact France-side mechanism with HEC and Bocconi student services before the student leaves India; both schools' public pages are silent on it.
exact_quote: Acceptance of your mobility allows you to continue your studies in France without the need to obtain a French residence card for a period of 360 days maximum and within the validity period of the residence permit held in the other EU member state.

title: Build the proof-of-funds file at the NEW threshold: EUR 877.50/month
duration_realistic: 1-3 weeks to assemble; do it before opening the Etudes en France file
what_happens: From 1 August 2026 the minimum resources a student visa applicant must evidence rose from EUR 615/month to EUR 877.50/month - about EUR 10,530 for a twelve-month stay. The threshold is set as a percentage of the gross SMIC and is now revised by ministerial order at least annually, so it will move again. France does NOT require a blocked account: service-public.fr accepts a bank attestation showing a sufficient credit balance, three recent payslips if the student works, a scholarship certificate, or third-party support (the sponsor's ID plus bank attestations of scheduled regular transfers, or a sworn attestation to pay the EUR 877.50/month). Multiple sources can be combined, but each one needs its own supporting document. Tuition paid in advance does not substitute for it - this is living-cost money on top of EUR 14,000-23,900/year of fees.
the_trap: The 43% jump is the highest-value fact in this entire chain and it is barely eighteen months old. Every guide, agent spreadsheet and school page written before August 2026 still says EUR 615/month - Sciences Po's own students' site still carries the EUR 615 figure in its EU-mobility section as of 14 September 2026. A file built to EUR 615 is roughly EUR 3,150 short over a year and is a clean refusal. Second trap: a lump sum sitting in a parent's account with no attestation of scheduled transfers is weaker than a modest sum with a documented standing arrangement.
exact_quote: Vous devez pouvoir justifier de ressources au moins egales a 877,5 EUR par mois. [inde.campusfrance.org: 'Effective 1 August 2026, the minimum proof of financial resources required for a French student visa will be revised to 877,5EUR/month.']

title: Budget the full cash stack - it is not just tuition
duration_realistic: Spread across 6-9 months
what_happens: For an Indian student entering one of these eight, the non-tuition cash calls in sequence are: application fee EUR 100-150 per school (Sciences Po EUR 150, Polytechnique EUR 105, EDHEC EUR 100, ESSEC EUR 100); enrolment deposit EUR 5,000 (EDHEC) or EUR 5,500 (ESSEC) within about two weeks of admission; Etudes en France fee INR 20,000; long-stay student visa fee EUR 50; VFS India service charge; VLS-TS validation tax EUR 100 after arrival; CVEC EUR 105 at enrolment; then EUR 877.50/month of evidenced living funds. Tuition itself runs EUR 14,000/year plus a EUR 2,000 one-off service fee (SKEMA), EUR 15,500/year (emlyon), EUR 14,900/year (Sciences Po non-EEA), EUR 15,900 or 23,900/year (EDHEC), EUR 19,600/year (Polytechnique non-EU), and EUR 23,000 rising to EUR 26,500/year (HEC x Bocconi). ESSEC does not publish a public per-year figure.
the_trap: The deposit lands before the visa exists and is non-refundable; the EEF fee is non-refundable; the application fee is non-refundable ('this fee is non-refundable' - Sciences Po). A family that plans only for tuition faces roughly EUR 5,500-6,000 of unrecoverable spend before a consulate has looked at the file. Note also the HEC x Bocconi fee discrepancy between sources: HEC's page shows EUR 26,500 for Year 2 (2027/28) while Bocconi's own fee page shows EUR 25,750 - budget to the higher figure.
exact_quote: Tuition fees are 14,900 EUR per academic year (non-EEA household tax residence); application fee '150 EUR (this fee is non-refundable)'.

title: Open the Etudes en France (EEF) file - MANDATORY even though these are private schools
institutions: All 7 France-based programmes (not HEC x Bocconi Year 1, which is Italy)
duration_realistic: 1-2 weeks to build and submit; add 1-3 weeks for anomaly corrections
what_happens: This is the question that decides the whole timeline, and the answer is yes. India is one of the ~73 countries covered by the Etudes en France procedure, and EEF is a PRE-CONSULAR step, not an admissions portal - it gates the visa, not the offer. Sciences Po, Ecole Polytechnique, EDHEC, ESSEC, SKEMA and emlyon are 'non-connected' institutions: the student applies on the school's own portal, is admitted by the school, and only then creates an EEF account at pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/etudesenfrance selecting the 'I have already gotten admission' route. Campus France then reviews the file, flags anomalies for correction, and validates it. The EEF file carries academic records, language evidence, CV and statement of purpose. Sciences Po's own guidance tells students to do exactly this: check whether the home country is covered by EEF and if so apply through Campus France.
the_trap: Believing the widely-repeated claim that the grandes ecoles and business schools are 'exempt from Campus France'. They are exempt from EEF as an APPLICATION route - the admission genuinely happens on the school's portal - but not from EEF as a VISA route. VFS will not process a long-stay student visa without the Campus France step behind it. The sequencing consequence is the one that costs intakes: EEF cannot be opened until the unconditional acceptance letter exists, so a March or June admission leaves very little runway. The genuine exemptions are narrow: French government scholarship holders (Eiffel, Charpak, MOPGA), certain co-financed scholarship holders, and short stays under 90 days.
exact_quote: In order to obtain a long stay student visa, the first step is to complete the Etudes en France (EEF) mandatory procedure. [ghana.campusfrance.org: 'After gaining admission, you must create an account on the EEF platform indicating I have already gotten admission.']

title: Pay the Etudes en France fee - now INR 20,000
duration_realistic: Same day; declare the payment on the portal immediately
what_happens: Once Campus France validates the file, the student pays the EEF processing fee and declares the payment on the platform. The fee rose from INR 18,500 to INR 20,000 with effect from 1 August 2026, so INR 20,000 is the live figure as of 14 September 2026. It is payable even when the institution is not connected to the platform, because the fee covers the pre-consular visa processing rather than any school application review. It is non-refundable and is charged per campaign, not per institution. French government and certain co-financed scholarship holders are exempt from the fee and from the procedure.
the_trap: Paying and then forgetting to DECLARE the payment on the EEF portal - the file does not advance until the declaration is recorded, and students lose a fortnight assuming Campus France can see the transaction. The second trap is budgeting the old INR 18,500.
exact_quote: The Etudes en France (EEF) fees will increase from INR 18,500 to INR 20,000, effective from 1st August 2026.

title: Attend the Campus France academic interview in India
duration_realistic: 2-4 weeks' wait for the allotted slot
what_happens: After the payment declaration, Campus France India allots an interview slot. Campus France India's own instruction is that the student appears IN PERSON, brings originals of all documents, and explains the study project - why France, why this school, why this programme, and how it is funded. Campus France India's page is explicit that no NOC is issued: what follows a successful interview is an automated email clearing the student to proceed to VFS, plus a Campus France file reference. That email is the gate - the VFS appointment cannot be booked before it arrives.
the_trap: Two failures. (1) Students book the VFS appointment early 'to be safe' and lose it, because the appointment can only be booked after the clearance email. (2) Students prepare for the interview as a formality. For these eight programmes it is the opposite: a student who cannot explain why they are paying EUR 23,900 a year at EDHEC rather than a cheaper public option, or who picked a Sciences Po campus without knowing it decides the regional minor and the language of instruction, gives Campus France a weak study project - and a weak project is the standard reason these files stall.
exact_quote: You will be required to appear in person for the academic interview with the Campus France as per the slot allotted to you. It is mandatory to bring originals of all necessary documents... After the interview, you will get an automated email stating that you can proceed to VFS. Important: Campus France does not issue any NOC.

title: File the VLS-TS application on France-Visas and submit at VFS India
duration_realistic: Appointment day, after a 1-4 week wait for a slot
what_happens: The student completes the visa application on france-visas.gouv.fr, generates the receipt, then books and attends a VFS Global appointment (14 centres across India) for biometrics and document submission. The visa sought is the long-stay visa acting as a residence permit - VLS-TS mention 'etudiant' - valid from 4 months to 1 year. The visa fee for students from EEF countries is EUR 50, a reduced rate against the EUR 99 standard long-stay fee, plus VFS's own non-refundable service charge. The file carries the passport, the unconditional acceptance letter, the Campus France clearance, proof of EUR 877.50/month, accommodation evidence for the arrival period, and travel booking. Campus France India's rule is to apply as soon as the unconditional acceptance letter arrives and at least three months before the intake; applications cannot be lodged more than six months ahead.
the_trap: Accommodation proof is the quiet blocker. The file wants an address in France before the student has a lease, and French landlords will not sign for someone without a visa - a circular problem Step 19 solves. A hotel booking, a student-residence certificate or a housing contract is accepted, and Sciences Po will issue a certificate to support the application if asked. Second trap: VFS service charges are non-refundable even on refusal.
exact_quote: You will also pay a visa application fee of 50 EUR (approximately $58) for your long-stay visa upon filing your application.

title: Visa processing - budget 2 to 3 months, not the advertised two weeks
duration_realistic: 2-3 months from submission; the whole admission-to-visa span is realistically 3-5 months
what_happens: Sciences Po tells its own admitted students plainly that 'a visa request may take 2 to 3 months' and to book the appointment the moment admission is confirmed. Campus France India's instruction points the same way: submit as soon as the unconditional acceptance letter arrives and at least three months before the intake date. Stacked end to end - EEF file build, anomaly corrections, fee and declaration, interview slot, VFS slot, decision - the realistic span from admission letter to visa in hand is three to five months for a September intake.
the_trap: Working backwards from the September start instead of forwards from the admission date. A Sciences Po Round 3 result in early May 2027 or an EDHEC Round 5 result on 2 July 2027 leaves two to four months for a chain that needs three to five - which is why the early rounds in Step 5 matter more in France than in most systems. Visas are granted at the sole discretion of the French consular authorities; there is no appeal that fits inside an intake.
exact_quote: Make sure that you make an appointment as soon as you have received confirmation of your admission to Sciences Po. A visa request may take 2 to 3 months.

title: Validate the VLS-TS online within 3 months of arrival - the step students forget
duration_realistic: 30 minutes online, but it MUST happen inside the first 3 months
what_happens: The VLS-TS is a visa that becomes a residence permit only once it is validated. Within three months of arriving, the student validates it on the Ministry of the Interior's ANEF portal (administration-etrangers-en-france.interieur.gouv.fr/particuliers/) and pays a tax of EUR 100 on top of the visa fee already paid. This replaced the old physical OFII appointment; there is no medical visit and no stamp in the passport for most students. Once validated, the VLS-TS acts as the residence permit for the first year of the stay.
the_trap: This is the single most-forgotten step in the French chain, because nothing chases the student - no letter, no summons, no school reminder. An unvalidated VLS-TS means the student is not in regular residence: they cannot re-enter the Schengen area after travelling (so the December trip home to India becomes the moment it is discovered), cannot get the Visale guarantee or CAF housing benefit cleanly, and faces a difficult conversation at the prefecture when the Year 2 permit is applied for. Note the figure carefully: the English-language version of service-public.fr shows EUR 150, which is the YEAR-TWO residence card cost (EUR 100 tax + EUR 50 stamp duty); the French original is explicit that the first-year VLS-TS validation is EUR 100.
exact_quote: Dans les 3 mois suivant votre arrivee en France, vous devez valider votre VLS-TS et payer une taxe qui s'ajoute aux droits de visa... Quel est le montant de la taxe a payer lors de la validation d'un VLS-TS 'etudiant' ? Il faut payer 100 EUR.

title: Pay the CVEC (EUR 105) BEFORE enrolling - private schools included
duration_realistic: 15 minutes online; can be done from India before departure
what_happens: The Contribution de vie etudiante et de campus is a compulsory annual contribution collected by the CROUS, paid at cvec.etudiant.gouv.fr by card (or in cash through the Nirio/FDJ network). For 2026-2027 it is EUR 105, unchanged from the previous year. Every student in initial higher education must obtain the attestation d'acquittement BEFORE registering at their institution, and the institution will ask for the attestation number during enrolment. Campus France is explicit that this applies to private institutions as well as public ones, which covers all seven France-based programmes in this dataset. Exemptions (refugees, subsidiary protection, asylum seekers, French government scholarship holders) still require logging in to obtain an exemption attestation. The 2026-2027 refund campaign runs to 31 May 2027.
the_trap: Students treat it as a university-only tax and skip it because they are going to a grande ecole or a business school - then cannot complete administrative registration in the first week of term. Beware stale figures: Campus France India's own arrival checklist still states 'The contribution to campus and student life costs 91 euros per year', a 2019-20 amount; the official CVEC portal shows EUR 105 for 2026-2027. Pay it as close as possible to the actual enrolment, and keep the attestation.
exact_quote: L'acquittement est actuellement possible pour l'annee universitaire 2026-2027. Elle est de 105 EUR euros... Chaque etudiant inscrit en formation initiale dans un etablissement d'enseignement superieur doit obligatoirement obtenir, prealablement a son inscription, son attestation d'acquittement.

title: Complete administrative registration at the school
duration_realistic: 1 day, in the 2 weeks before classes start
what_happens: The student accepts the offer online, completes administrative registration and course registration, collects the student card and settles the tuition schedule. Sciences Po's advice to international students is to arrive at least two weeks before classes begin so registration, banking and housing can be done without pressure. Non-EU students at EDHEC must settle tuition by wire transfer; direct debit is not open to them, which matters because a first Indian-to-French transfer can take several working days and may hit LRS documentation at the Indian end.
the_trap: Arriving on the first day of class. Registration needs the CVEC attestation, a French address and often a French bank RIB, and none of those exists on day one. Sciences Po explicitly recommends a two-week buffer; students who book flights to the orientation date compress registration, banking, health cover and housing into the same week as their first lectures.
exact_quote: We recommend that you arrive at least two weeks before classes start so you have time to complete all your administrative formalities without getting stressed.

title: Register with the French health system (free, and not optional)
duration_realistic: 2-8 weeks for the provisional social security number after filing
what_happens: Affiliation to the French social security system is free and compulsory for non-EU students staying more than three months. Once the school has issued the enrolment certificate, the student registers at etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr, uploads the residence document and supporting papers, and is issued a provisional social security number, then an ameli account and an attestation de droits. The follow-on steps are ordering the carte Vitale, declaring a medecin traitant (which raises the reimbursement rate) and taking out a complementary mutuelle for the unreimbursed share. EU/EEA students with a European Health Insurance Card do not register here at all.
the_trap: Students buy an expensive private Indian travel-health policy for the whole year believing French cover costs money, or delay registration because the carte Vitale takes weeks. Registration cannot start until the enrolment certificate exists, so there is a genuine uncovered gap between landing and registration - bridge it with short-term travel cover, not with a year-long policy that duplicates free statutory cover.
exact_quote: Membership in the French social security system is free and compulsory... Once you have arrived in France and been issued with your certificate of enrollment by a French institute of higher education, you will be able to register on l'Assurance Maladie's dedicated website, etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr.

title: Housing and the guarantor problem - use Visale
duration_realistic: Start 4-6 months before arrival; the Visale visa itself takes days and is valid 6 months
what_happens: French private landlords almost always demand a garant - a French-resident third party who contractually covers the rent - and an Indian family cannot supply one. Visale is the state-backed answer: a free guarantee from Action Logement that stands as guarantor to the landlord. The student creates an account at visale.fr, requests a 'visa Visale' with two documents (ID and proof of student status), and hands the certified visa to the landlord or the university residence. For students the Visale visa is valid six months, so a student targeting a 1 September move-in can request it from 1 April. Non-EU students are eligible only if they can evidence a student-category visa, and only between 18 and 30 inclusive. Once installed, most students can also claim CAF housing benefit (APL).
the_trap: The eligibility gate is circular and catches almost everyone: Visale requires a student visa, the visa file wants a French address, and the landlord wants a guarantor. The way out is a short-term booking (hotel, Airbnb, CROUS or school residence) for the visa file and the first weeks, then Visale for the real lease. Also note the rent ceilings are contested across official sources: etudiant.gouv.fr still publishes the old caps of EUR 800 in Ile-de-France and EUR 600 elsewhere on a page dated 2021, while the scheme was restructured in January 2026 into three geographic zones with substantially higher student caps. Check the live eligibility tester on visale.fr before promising a student a given flat is covered.
exact_quote: Ce service est propose gratuitement par Action Logement et garantit au bailleur (proprietaire) de percevoir le loyer en cas de non-paiement du locataire... Seuls les etudiants entre 18 a 30 ans inclus sont eligibles. Les etudiants etrangers hors Union europeenne sont eligibles s'ils peuvent justifier d'un visa mention etudiant.

title: Year 2 onward: convert the VLS-TS into a carte de sejour before it expires
institutions: All 7 France-based programmes (these are 3-4 year degrees, so every student hits this)
duration_realistic: Apply 4 to 2 months before the VLS-TS expires
what_happens: The VLS-TS covers only the first year. The application for the carte de sejour temporaire etudiant (1 year) or pluriannuelle etudiant (2-4 years) must be filed at the earliest 4 months and at the latest 2 months before the current document expires, through the ANEF portal or the prefecture. The file re-tests the same resources condition of EUR 877.50/month, plus the previous year's transcripts, the enrolment certificate, and a signed undertaking to respect the principles of the Republic. The cost is EUR 150 in fiscal stamps (EUR 100 tax + EUR 50 stamp duty). The prefecture also assesses the 'caractere reel et serieux' of the studies - attendance, exam results, progression.
the_trap: Filing late. Service-public.fr is explicit that a late renewal adds a EUR 180 regularisation visa fee on top, except in cases of force majeure. With four-year BBAs at EDHEC, ESSEC, SKEMA and emlyon this cycle repeats three times, and a failed or repeated year feeds directly into the 'real and serious studies' assessment.
exact_quote: Vous devez demander votre titre de sejour au plus tot 4 mois et au plus tard 2 mois avant la fin de validite de votre document de sejour... Vous devez regler 150 EUR (100 EUR de taxe + 50 EUR de droit de timbre) par timbres fiscaux... Si vous presentez votre demande de renouvellement de titre hors delai, vous devrez aussi payer un droit de visa de regularisation de 180 EUR.

title: Sciences Po only: plan the compulsory Year 3 abroad around the residence permit
duration_realistic: Plan from the end of Year 1
what_happens: The Sciences Po Bachelor of Arts has a compulsory third year of international mobility - the student leaves France for a full academic year and returns for nothing, since the BA ends there, or continues to a master's. That year abroad has to be reconciled with a French residence permit that assumes continuous residence. Sciences Po's own guidance notes that where a programme includes compulsory mobility within the European Union, the student must present a certificate from the university to the consulate in order to obtain a student mobility visa, and can then apply for a multi-year 'student - mobility programme' residence permit.
the_trap: Treating the year abroad as a school matter and not an immigration one. A student who lets the French permit lapse while abroad, or who leaves on a one-year permit with no mobility endorsement, can face a fresh consular application to come back - and the destination country's own visa sits on top. Raise it at the end of Year 1, not in the summer before departure.
exact_quote: If your program includes a compulsory mobility within the European Union, you will need to present to the consulate a certificate from the university allowing you to obtain a student mobility visa. You will then be able to apply for a multi-year residence permit 'student - mobility program.'

title: EU/EEA/Swiss shortcut (one line)
duration_realistic: n/a
what_happens: An EU, EEA or Swiss national needs no visa, no Etudes en France file, no Campus France fee and no VLS-TS validation - they apply on the school's portal, pay the CVEC, enrol, and use an EHIC instead of registering at etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr; Visale and CAF remain available. At Sciences Po they also pay income-banded fees from EUR 0 to EUR 14,900 rather than the flat non-EEA rate, and at Polytechnique EUR 15,900 rather than EUR 19,600.
the_trap: None material - but note Sciences Po's fee band follows household FISCAL RESIDENCE, not nationality, so an EU passport held by a family tax-resident outside the EEA still pays the full EUR 14,900.
exact_quote: Citizens of European Union countries, the European Economic Area or Switzerland do not need a visa to study in France.
